review.note: Reviewed all direct build, runtime, optional-development and Node registry candidates, including candidates outside declared bounds, against the committed 0.24.1 receipt. Every non-Core latest version, Python 3.14 support result and declaration is unchanged; the prior official release-note reviews retained in Git history remain applicable. The registry Core latest has advanced from 0.42.2 to 0.44.0, which this range already admits and the previous release validated. Independently reviewed the local Core 0.44-to-0.45 release diff ending at merge 0ec9a49: it changes bounded ingest decision loading and performance telemetry, including a breaking telemetry record format, but does not change the public catalog and readonly administration contracts used by OPDS. OPDS does not consume the changed telemetry format. The consumer now admits h2hdb>=0.43.0,<0.46.0; schema-8 releases and the next unreviewed 0.46 lane remain excluded. Core 0.45.0 was supplied explicitly as wheel SHA256 255180d5bd152b4744a6f3932f354e110e6b621c86f211854978780089ffc8ba, and all 95 installed package files match that wheel. This is not a claim that Core 0.45.0 is available from the registry. Normal dependency resolution installed the candidate in the OPDS development environment, and 10 targeted cases passed with Core 0.45.0: publication timestamp HTTP serialization, genuine schema-9 SQLite vertical slice, built-wheel dependency boundaries, and readonly startup admission/failure cleanup. A separate clean venv normally resolved and installed the OPDS 0.24.2 wheel together with the explicit Core 0.45.0 wheel, without --no-deps or a development-site .pth; uv pip check passed, both imports came from that venv, and installed-wheel CLI, /version and OpenAPI checks passed. Functional-commit Ruff, formatting, strict mypy and Markdown checks passed. No runtime shim, migration, OPDS HTTP contract, library representation, or data format was changed. Existing schema 9 needs no conversion, deletion or CBZ/artwork rebuild. The final exact-tree full merge gate and distribution smoke remain mandatory and are not claimed by this dependency receipt. All execution was local; no NAS, live external consumer account or production database was used.
